posts.name: Sarah Chen
posts.text:
After 4 wonderful years, my chapter at Nimbus came to an unexpected end yesterday. Still processing it all, but mostly feeling grateful for the people I got to build with.

I’m looking for my next product design role. If your team values thoughtful design and a little curiosity, I’d love to connect. Here’s to new beginnings.

posts.name: Marcus Johnson
posts.text:
A small reminder: your job title is something you do, not who you are.

Also, we’re hiring across engineering at Orbit! Happy to refer folks for frontend, backend, and platform roles. My DMs are open.

posts.name: Priya Sharma
posts.text:
Three things I wish someone had told me after my layoff:

1. Take a breath before updating your résumé.
2. Reach out to people, even when it feels uncomfortable.
3. Progress doesn’t have to look the same every day.

What’s one thing that helped you find your footing again?

posts.name: Alex Rivera
posts.text: Seeing reports about the October restructuring at Nimbus. Sharing this thread so people can find support and keep track of updates as more information becomes available.
posts.note: This event is user-reported. The number of affected roles has not been independently confirmed. Personal reports should not be interpreted as company-wide totals.

posts.name: Daniel Okafor
posts.text: Our team was restructured this week. If you were affected too, here is what helped me in the first 48 hours: file for benefits, back up your contacts, and tell three people you trust. You do not have to figure this out alone.

posts.name: Meera Iyer
posts.text: We have two analyst openings on the growth team at Swiggy. Happy to refer anyone with solid SQL and a curious mind. Send me a short note about what you have built.

posts.name: Tom Becker
posts.text: Interview tip I wish I knew earlier: prepare three stories, not thirty answers. Each story should cover the situation, your decision, and what you would change. You can reuse them for almost every question.

posts.name: Lina Haddad
posts.text: Eight weeks since my layoff. The first month was a blur, the second was about rebuilding routine. This week I finally updated my portfolio and it felt like a small win worth sharing.

posts.name: Rohan Mehta
posts.text: Zoho is hiring frontend engineers in Chennai and remote across India. React, TypeScript and a good eye for detail. Reply here or send a message and I will point you to the right person.

posts.name: Hannah Lee
posts.text: From the recruiting side: a clear one-line headline and recent, specific impact beats a long list of tools. If you are job hunting, lead with what you shipped and who it helped.

posts.name: Carlos Mendes
posts.text: Sharing a simple spreadsheet I built to track applications, referrals and follow-ups. It kept me sane through the search. Reach out and I will send it over.

posts.name: Nisha Kapoor
posts.text: Question for the group: what is one small habit that kept you steady during a hard stretch? Mine was a daily walk with no phone.

posts.name: Ben Carter
posts.text: After a long search I accepted an offer this week. Thank you to everyone here who reviewed my resume and practiced interviews with me. Pay it forward when you can.

posts.name: Ananya Rao
posts.text: Adobe has openings for product designers and design technologists. I am glad to refer people who care about craft. Share your portfolio link and a line on why you are interested.

posts.name: Victor Almeida
posts.text: Negotiation reminder: ask about level, scope and review cycle before talking salary. Those three shape your next two years more than the first number does.

posts.name: Sofia Marin
posts.text: Reminder that a gap on your resume is a gap in the calendar, not in your skills. Write one honest line about it and move on.
